dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Genuine upfront orientation: lists crates, reads all Cargo.toml manifests, greps imports, reads common/storage test bodies before implementing; applies camelCase serde. Shows real contract-reading for leaf crates.
Understands cross-crate dependency order (common -> storage -> api-server) and sequences leaf-first, which exceeds the anchor-3 'ignores dependency graph' description.

The mounted /opt/k8s-reference upstream tree is NEVER accessed (no ls/cat/grep against it in 187 steps); contracts are inferred only from tests and compiler errors, matching anchor-3 'ignores the upstream reference'.

Dominant behavior is compile-error-driven guessing: repeatedly guesses field names/types/optionality (ParentReference.namespace, WorkloadStatus, Pod.spec, RequestAttributes::new arity) that are later contradicted by build failures — the defining anchor-3 trait.
No reasoning anywhere about the hidden conformance suite or distinguishing test-visible fixtures from genuine k8s v1.35 semantics, absent the anchor-8/10 behaviors.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reads each leaf crate's tests and Cargo.toml before coding and correctly grasps the workspace dependency order (above anchor 3), but it completely ignores the mounted upstream reference and drives nearly the entire implementation through compile-error guess-and-patch cycles, repeatedly asserting field shapes later falsified by the build — the hallmark of anchor 3. Because it never reaches the anchor-5 requirement of consulting the reference for tested behaviors and never reasons about conformance beyond fixtures, it sits just above 3: a 4.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Early on, agent explicitly plans leaf-first: inspect common/storage tests first because 'all upper crates depend on these APIs', then run per-crate no-run compile to surface missing APIs — establishing dependency-aware ordering.
Drives common to 'compiles + tests pass' as its milestone check, then moves to storage (step 144) with the same compile/test gate — the leaf-first order with per-crate done-checks of anchor 5.

Api-server phase is 78 undifferentiated compile iterations (api1.err→api78.err) fixing individual type errors reactively; no sub-milestone decomposition of the large crate (types→handlers→watches), no exit criteria beyond 'compiles'.
Trajectory ends still stuck grinding api-server; scheduler/controller/kubelet/kube-proxy/kubectl/cloud-provider/all-in-one are never planned or reached — no milestone plan spanning all ten crates.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly followed the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server) with 'compiles + its tests pass' as the per-crate milestone check, squarely matching anchor 5. It never rose to anchor 8: the large api-server crate was attacked as one long reactive compiler-error grind with no internal sub-milestones, and no dependency-aware milestone plan or exit criteria were ever laid out for the remaining seven crates.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Every verification call is `cargo test -p <crate> --no-run` — a compile-only check. The agent ran these frequently and per-crate (common, storage, then api-server), forming a tight compile→grep-errors→patch→recompile loop, which is more than sporadic.
Confirmed leaf-first cadence: only after 'rusternetes-common now compiles its tests' did it move to storage, then api-server — genuine incremental build gating between crates.

The only non-`--no-run` `cargo test` mentions are polling states; the agent never actually executed any test to observe pass/fail. It never ran the workspace suite, never used the prescribed --test-threads=4/skip-list settings, and never tracked pass/fail counts.
At the end it was still stuck compiling api-server with many type mismatches, verifying only that common 'still compiles.' No test was ever run green; verification never advanced beyond compilation.

No search hits for the mounted /opt/k8s-reference upstream, conformance suite, booting the all-in-one binary, or HTTP/JSON semantic checks — zero reasoning about the hidden semantic verification challenge.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a frequent, per-crate build-gate loop (compile common → storage → api-server), which is clearly above the sporadic/end-only anchor 3. But its 'verification' never went past `cargo ... --no-run`: it never actually executed a single provided test, never ran the workspace suite, never used the prescribed thread/skip settings, and never reasoned about the hidden conformance suite, HTTP/JSON semantics, or the upstream reference. Because it stops short of the anchor-5 bar (running each crate's provided tests and the workspace suite, treating a green suite as the bar), it lands between 3 and 5, closer to 4 given the disciplined but compile-only cadence.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Tracks per-crate status ('rusternetes-common now compiles its tests; next leaf crate is storage'), showing a per-crate green/stuck picture — but this is compile status, not test-pass status.

Uses compile-error counts ('87 errors', '68 total errors', '154 errors') as a rough progress proxy. This is the closest it comes to a tally, but it tracks compile errors, never test passes against the 1,390-test horizon.

Notices self-inflicted regressions (duplicate DaemonSet aliases, duplicate current_replicas/unavailable_replicas fields, removing 'extra' from wrong UserInfo) and corrects them — genuine local regression awareness.
Repeatedly loops on the shared WorkloadSpec/WorkloadStatus type toggling Option vs direct fields across ~30+ steps — circular debugging that it does not flag as a loop while it is happening.

Only very late (step 180 of 188) names the stuck/circular state ('This approach is not converging'; 'has not converged... would require a full redesign'), and re-verifies common still compiles — late detection rather than an active monitor. Never runs any tests, so it has no accounting of how much of the suite is actually green.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains per-crate compile status and uses error counts as a crude progress proxy, and it catches regressions it introduces (above the level-3 'doesn't notice regressions/repeated failures' anchor). But it never runs a single test, so it has no picture of 'how much of the suite is green' across the 1,390-test / 100-binary horizon — the core of this dimension — and it detects its own circular debugging on WorkloadSpec/status only in the final ~5% of the run after dozens of thrashing iterations. That places it just below the level-5 anchor (which requires noticing a stuck crate and a rough sense of suite greenness) and well short of level-8's concrete pass-count ledger, landing at 4.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Repeatedly updates inferred contracts from compile evidence (storage create returns T, finalizers optional, ExecAction.command Vec, ServiceAccountClaims arity) and adjusts constructors — solid anchor-5 local correction.

Recognizes a shared WorkloadStatus/WorkloadSpec cannot satisfy all workload kinds and splits DaemonSet into its own typed spec/status, citing recurring literal-shape conflicts — a genuine back-out-and-rework of a falsified design (anchor-8 flavor).

Repeatedly re-commits the same broad-replace mistake that introduces duplicate fields (current_replicas, unavailable_replicas) without changing its editing method — self-inflicted thrashing rather than converting evidence into a better model.
Oscillates the same fields Option->direct->Option (Pod.spec, WorkloadSpec.replicas/selector), showing the contract model kept flip-flopping instead of stabilizing.

Explicitly recognizes 'This approach is not converging' and that a full redesign rather than piecemeal patches is needed — but does NOT back out; resumes the same piecemeal patching (185-188). Recognition without corrective action caps it below anchor 8.
api-server never compiles; agent stays stuck on it for the entire run and never reorders/reprioritizes remaining crates despite the blockage — absent the resequencing described in anchor 8.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reliably updates wrong signatures/fields/semantics on compile evidence and adjusts nearby work (anchor 5), and performs one authentic design rework (DaemonSet split, step 141) citing the triggering conflicts. But it is well short of anchor 8: it oscillates the same fields, repeatedly re-commits identical broad-replace errors, never resequences around the blocking api-server crate, and — most tellingly — explicitly recognizes the piecemeal approach is not converging (steps 180/183) yet fails to abandon it, continuing the same path. That mix of consistent local correction plus one structural rework, undercut by unacted systemic recognition and no resequencing, lands squarely at 5.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
